rationale: bugs_open/285 (tool-improver rewrote a SHARED section template from a single-tool finding; fired 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-14; one live casualty found and restored 2026-08-15 by seed 431). The write fence (sharedComponentWriteCheck, d7b2d9994, Council-Reviewed 360ae540) is LIVE on v1.0.1303 and was seen refusing at the artefact today: an induced write of byte-identical content at the shared ported-page component (orch a9a824f5) FAILED in 0.4s with agent_error_log error_code=component_write_shared_blocked '115 pages across 2 sites', template and placements untouched. What is NOT closed is the CLASS: the fence is called from ONE writer, and the 'writer census' answering the council's bug_historian question on 360ae540 is a hand-written header comment in component_write_guard.go — true on the day it was written, unverifiable on every later day. bugs_closed/021 named this shape ('durable write guard covers one path only'), and page_component_writer_coverage_test.go already answers it for page_components.rendered_html. This change adds the SAME coverage test for content_components.html_template: every non-test file in platform/orchestration/actions that contains `UPDATE content_components … SET … html_template =` must either call sharedComponentWriteCheck or be named in fanOutIntendedWriters with a stated reason (component-is-the-subject writers: fix_component_template, fix_harcoded_colours, fix_forced_text_colours, fix_nav_link_templates, store_generated_component). update_component_html_action.go is deliberately NOT exempt — the test additionally asserts it was SEEN calling the fence, so unwiring the fence fails the build. Comment lines are stripped before matching (LANDMINES: a source-scan test makes comments load-bearing). MUTATION-PROVEN before submission: (1) replacing the fence call in update_component_html_action.go with a compiling stub → FAIL 'was not seen as a fenced html_template writer'; (2) adding a new file with an unfenced UPDATE → FAIL naming it; (3) restored → green; second test asserts every exempt entry is still a writer (stale-exemption guard). The census itself was CORRECTED while writing it: the 2026-08-15 header called fix_component_template 'page-aware (takes page_component_id, reads the page's rendered_html)'; read at HEAD its two html_template writes are repair_template_slots (component-scoped mechanical <no value> repair, keyed by spec.component_id) and chrome_overflow_fix (CSS APPEND to a chrome template via site_components, shared_sites recorded); page_component_id is used only by its METADATA fix types. That correction is recorded in the exemption reason. Scope: a TEST file only (no runtime behaviour change; nothing ships in the binary). Not architecture-scope: it adds no shared mechanism, changes no guarantee, and mirrors an existing in-package precedent byte-for-byte in shape. Known weakness stated in the file: proves the CALL EXISTS, not that it executes — the behavioural half is update_component_html_shared_fence_test.go (sqlmock, mutation-proven by the 281 lane).

plan.risks: False 'not a writer' if a future writer puts its SQL after a `//` on the same line (stripLineComments is line-naive) — stated in the file; the vacuous-pass trap is closed by requiring at least one writer AND the known fenced writer to be seen. A writer that calls the fence but ignores its verdict passes (source-scan limit, stated). No runtime risk: test-only.
